requested_parts: whether setup Blight cascades or destroys Presence
answers.answer: Setup Blight comes from the box, never the pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence. The ordinary procedure applies only to Blight added after setup: it destroys one Presence per Spirit in the land and cascades one Blight to one adjacent land if the land was already Blighted.

evidence.text: Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.
After setup, take Blight added to the island from the active card/board pool. Whenever one or more Blight is added to a land:
1. Destroy **one Presence from each Spirit** with Presence there, not every disk and not just one disk total. Decrease each affected Spirit's Presence count in that land by exactly one.

2. If the land already had any Blight, **cascade**: also add **one** Blight to **one adjacent land** chosen by the players. Resolve its Presence loss and cascade if it was already Blighted. The amount of existing Blight does not multiply the cascade. Cascades can cross boards and remain part of the original action; revisiting a land destroys another disk per Spirit there and continues cascading.

answers.answer: Players may distribute Damage among Invaders however they wish; can split 1 to Town and 2 to City, so neither is destroyed.

evidence.text: “Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. Marked Damage does not reduce the Health counted by a Health-worth removal allowance. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. answers.answer: Select all pieces before simultaneous replacements, so the same City cannot be downgraded twice in that one instruction. Separate completed actions can replace the resulting piece again, such as successive players’ Trade Suffers.

evidence.text: **Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

answers.answer: Use printed Health; ignore Health modifiers.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. [Core: .7w4g8qy, .9v5kbka, .7w4g8pb, .9v5ka9g, .7w4g8r4, .9v5kfqb, .9v5kfqs, .7w4gdtl]

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Use printed Health; ignore Health modifiers.

answers.answer: Push the three Explorers to as many different legal destinations as possible, so with three available lands send one to each. If only two legal destination lands exist, use both and send the remaining Explorer to either legal destination; all three must be pushed.

evidence.text: - **Core Power specifics:** **Song of Sanctity** is Slow, despite missing cost-circle ink in some printings. Its printed condition selects the available instruction: if the target has any Explorers, Push all of them and the Blight-removal instruction is **unavailable**. If it has no Explorers, instead remove 1 Blight. The player does not choose between those branches. **Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship** line 3 Pushes all Explorers **to as many different lands as possible**, using every available legal destination up to the number of Explorers; its Invaders damaging each other do so simultaneously, **before** the Explorer Push as the threshold specifies. **Poisoned Land**'s threshold counts the Blight that its own earlier instruction added. **Tsunami**'s threshold adds Fear for each other Coastal land it affects. [Core: .7w4g9dg, .9v5kc31, .7w4ganc, .7w4g8q3, .7w4g8pc]

answers.answer: No fresh draw: using Spirit gains one of the same three cards target did not keep. In solo both gains come from the single four-card draw.

evidence.text: - **Entwined Power:** Shared Presence applies only to targeting (Range/source/target boxes), not to text effects or counting “your lands.” One disk each can count as a Sacred Site for their Power targeting, but is not a real shared site for Fear Cards or other effects. River's special Wetland-site rule remains River's own. For its base card gains, the **target Spirit** first makes the normal draw-four/keep-one gain; the **using Spirit** then gains one of those same three unkept cards, without drawing another four. In solo, both gains come from that single four-card draw. The threshold also lets the using and target Spirits each independently gift the other one Power Card **from hand**, optionally; cards in play or personal discard cannot be gifted by it. The threshold gives 6 Energy in solo; each Major gained still needs a separate Forget. If a transferred Unique references a special effect defined by a Spirit's rule, such as Drown, that definition still applies; skip instructions requiring a personal track you do not have. answers.answer: Yes. Powerstorm requires paying the repeated Power Card’s Energy cost again; original play payment does not cover Repeat.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Yes. Powerstorm requires paying the repeated Power Card’s Energy cost again; original play payment does not cover Repeat.
